en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kaḷambadāyaka Ekavihārivagga 6 I am a forest-dwelling monk, one who lives alone; I have gone forth into homelessness, seeking peace. I dwell in the forest, in a mountain cave, Free from fear, having abandoned all dread. In the past, during the time of Kassapa, the Buddha, I was a householder, living in a village. At that time, I gave a kaḷamba flower To the Teacher, the Great Sage, the Fully Enlightened One. Because of that meritorious deed, For ninety-one aeons I experienced happiness. Now, as a result of that very same gift, I have attained this state of peace. Having seen the fruit of my own merit, I rejoice in my own good fortune. May I never again fall into the lower realms; May I always be reborn in the higher worlds. Having paid homage to the Elder Kaḷambadāyaka, One should pay homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, The Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, Who possesses the ten powers and is endowed with the four bases of confidence. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Kaḷambadāyaka.
“The Sambuddha named Romasa was dwelling among the mountains;
With faith and with my own hands,
that gift which I gave back then, ninety-four aeons ago;
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of the Kaḷamba tree.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
... [as before] ... the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Kaḷambadāyaka Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Kaḷambadāyaka is the sixth.
